svg.text: Inductive: permanent, σ-bond polarisation · Electromeric: temporary, π-bond shift that appears only in presence of an attacking reagent
−I effect: Cl pulls σ electrons; the pull weakens with distance
charge on C1 > C2 > C3 > C4 (δ+ shown larger where stronger)
Electromeric effect: π electrons move completely to one atom when a reagent attacks
+E : shift towards the attacking reagent (electrophile E
adds to the carbon that gets the π pair)
E added; effect ends once the reagent is removed
−E : shift away from the attacking reagent (Nu
adds to carbon, π pair goes to oxygen)
Nu adds to C; O carries the negative charge
